quest.title: Your Past Is Like a Garden
quest.description: The life of sentient beings seems destined to be a treacherous road. Yet, the warm and gentle sunshine still illuminates us who look upon one another. Yet deep and enduring love exists that can help us find ourselves again. And after the crisis passes, the flowers will be there to embrace you.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x875, Primogem x30, Mora x38100, Hero's Wit x4, Mystic Enhancement Ore x7

chapter.num: Song of the Welkin Moon: Act X
chapter.title: Of Myriad Paths, Flux, and Dissolution

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: ...Well, that's the last of them. Everyone on the list is already back where they should be.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It was a long, hard road, but we've finally finished escorting everyone back.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: I just pray that we'll never need to leave again. I hope we can stay here forever in this peaceful paradise of our own choosing.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Paradise... In the annals of the Temple of Silence, that word carries great significance. It represents the hopes and desires of the gods — their longing for a place to rest.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: I wouldn't think gods need such a place.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: People always think they're the only ones who can lose their homes. They forget that gods, too, need a place to reside.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: As the Goat King once said, "A god without his people shall cease to exist." Gods need their believers every bit as much as their believers need them.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Only we can truly understand how much the desert faith has faded over the centuries. But we still talk about the gods as though they're a part of our lives.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Given the myriad ways in which gods and humans interact, I'd say they really are. How else could Dunyarzad consider the Dendro Archon a friend?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Well, that sounds about right to me. Describing them as "friends" sure makes us feel a whole lot closer.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Hah... If you'd told me a few years back that I'd have this many friends, I'd have called you a liar.

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Belief is a choice, just like friendship. We've made our choices through battle — the right ones, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I'll be heading back to the Temple of Silence. I heard the Goat King and the Ibis King decided to pay us a visit. How about you?

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: It's back to Aaru Village for us. Still plenty of supplies to distribute and people to help.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Until next time, old friend. As long as you can find the time, you're always welcome to visit us in Aaru Village.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Right back atcha. Make sure to drop by the Temple of Silence the next time you're free.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Word is that two of the other Seven Pillars, Shesepankh and Bennu, might also be dropping by. Since you're wearing the symbols of their power, it'd only be fitting if you came to see them for yourselves.

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: "Dropping by"? That makes it sound like they're visiting a neighbor's home...

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: Well, the Temple was founded by Hermanubis, so I guess to them, that's exactly what it is...

dialogues.speaker: Dehya
dialogues.text: Guess that's true...

dialogues.speaker: Candace
dialogues.text: Alright, we'll make sure to find time to stop by. Stay safe on your journey home.

dialogues.speaker: Sethos
dialogues.text: I will.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Hmm, you do have a point.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: See? Retirement has always been a problem, especially for old timers like us who've been locked away all these years. You finally step out into the light, and bam! You're face to face with a whole different world.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Naturally.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: What do you think, Layla?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Huh? ...W—Why would you think to ask me? Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: How could I possibly be qualified to decide where the servants of King Deshret should live...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Sorry if my question was unclear. Do you think their statues will stand out too much if we place them here?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Hey, I never agreed to this! How could we possibly allow our statues to be left in Hermanubis's home? That would be like... breaking into someone's house, then pretending it belonged to you in the first place!

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Different beliefs can coexist. We still need to respect one another.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: By which you mean, you two plan to stay at the Temple of Silence — for a while, at least — but you have no intention of relocating your statues here...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hmm... So you see this as sort of a family visit. Is that correct?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Family... Huh...

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: You could say that. In a sense, Hermanubis would view this as his home.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Just look at this place — magnificent, is it not? *sigh* The sad truth is, in the past, all three of us invested so much into misguided ventures. We failed to build what we should have... and wasted so much time instead.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: ...And, what do you mean by that?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: I mean that for the most part, time spent associating with the likes of Sobek — and, let's say, Thoth — might reasonably be considered wasted...

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Why does that not surprise me... *sigh* Go on.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Anyway, given how much time we'll all be spending together, I'd say that the bonds we built will end up proving to have been a sound investment.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Once Sethos, the current leader of the Temple of Silence, returns, you can discuss the matter of staying here with him.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: But, judging by the expressions of everyone here, I imagine you'll receive a very warm welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This sacred ground houses untold knowledge, after all. What better place for the servants of King Deshret to appear in the mortal world?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: How about we share a meal together first? I imagine it's been many years since you last tasted fresh food.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Oh, that sounds wonderful. After so many hundreds of years, I can only surmise that desert cuisine has become a lot more varied.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Are we having a get-together? If you'd like, I can help prepare some food. After all, Lord Thoth, you helped me so much in the desert, and I still haven't properly thanked you.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Oh my, that would be wonderful! I'm touched that you still remember.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: How the times have changed. To the people of today, it seems the Ibis King has become a kind and passionate god.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: And you, Mr. Heryshaf? What kind of god do you wish to be?

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: To be honest, I haven't given it much thought. How about you, Dendro Archon? Do you have any hopes for your future?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Me... I'm very happy with my current life.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Forgive my bluntness... But you do not seem to derive your authority from majesty and might, like Lord Al-Ahmar. Clearly, your approach has its advantages — but also its dangers, don't you think?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I do, but projecting a majestic front doesn't really suit me. Besides, my relationship with others isn't simply one of a god and her people.

dialogues.speaker: Heryshaf
dialogues.text: Not putting on airs might earn you more adoration.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Exactly. Besides, I really like parties where everyone brings their own food, and we all come together to share. You should join us — I'm sure you'll find it fun.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Last time, when we got together for a picnic near the Avidya Forest, it was quite the occasion. Seeing as you're already here... how about we hold the next one in the desert?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Can we do that? Wouldn't Tighnari have to transport a ton of drinking water?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I can help out. Layla, would you like to join us next time?

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: Me? S—Sure!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: The more, the merrier. That way, we—

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Don't take this the wrong way, I just think you should know — when it comes to passing the time, chess is more our thing.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ahem... In that case, Dendro Archon, what do you say?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If I were to compete against you, I can't say with certainty I'd win, but I certainly wouldn't mind giving it a shot.

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Where's Sobek? I'm sure he'd be good for a few rounds. Cards, cards, cards... Haha, I'll always prefer chess.

dialogues.speaker: Layla
dialogues.text: I wonder what variant of chess we're talking here... Uhm, Mr. Thoth... Is there some sort of astrological significance to this game?

dialogues.speaker: Thoth
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm glad you brought that up! As long as the leader of the Temple of Silence agrees, we can search Hermanubis's place for books to teach you how to play.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Such devastation visited on Sumeru City... So many houses destroyed or damaged in the fighting. Who could have foreseen this...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Look at all of this... It's going to take me forever to tidy up! I suppose living below the Akademiya doesn't always work out to your advantage.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I would have thought a little appreciation of my sincerity and effort in helping to clean up this mess might be in order?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Helping? Effort!? This is your house — of course you should be putting in the effort! If anything, I'm the one who's helping.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: So, you see yourself as just a helper in this situation? I must admit, I'm rather shocked.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: If you're trying to say that since I live here too, I have an obligation to tidy up... Fine, I suppose I do... Wait a second, stop changing the subject!

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* Nevertheless...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: In the wake of a great storm, a missing roof is a predictable inconvenience.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Can you stop making it seem like I care more about this house than you do? Doesn't it upset you at all to see your home in this state?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I won't pretend it's ideal, but that's no reason to be upset.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: This is the roof over your head — your shelter from the cold! The furniture is scattered, the paintings have fallen off the walls, the windows are shattered. Don't you feel even a little disheartened?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: The way I see it, these problems are easily solved.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Ugh, this is precisely why I hate talking to you about sentimental things. It's like banging my head against a wall! *sigh* You simply don't understand just how much work goes into making a proper home...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: It sounds like this is causing you a lot of anguish.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You mean the house, or the paintings?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I mean your sentimentality.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Oh, well, yes... But I'd rather not dwell on such things right now.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Generally speaking, when anguish becomes the norm, people usually make an attempt to improve their situation.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: But there are so many people and things in life that are difficult to change. It's not like you can force them. Besides...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...Anguish can be a source of inspiration, and I'm... not sure I could break my reliance on it...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: I'm glad you're able to make yourself think like that.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: ...What kind of a response is that!? I was stating a profound truth about the very nature of art! Suffering is the cradle of all creation... Even you can't deny that.

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: And I wasn't trying to. I'm just happy for you, pure and simple. Can't you tell?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Happy about what?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Happy that you can always find an answer that backs up your views.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: You...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: More often than not, life is a process of running into problems and then searching for answers. Yours more than most...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Not everyone's so good at justifying things to themselves. It's something that you've been steadily mastering.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Hah... What about you, then? What skills have you been "mastering" lately?

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Pass me that box.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? Okay...

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: You may consider this my progress on the path to mastery.

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: W—What!?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Wait a second... Isn't that box... mine? Hey, it is! It must've fallen off that shelf. Alhaitham, those are my paints and inks!

dialogues.speaker: Alhaitham
dialogues.text: Would you like me to put it in your bedroom for you?

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: Huh? I mean, sure, if you don't mind...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: (What kind of "progress" is this? Does he think he can bribe me? Not that giving me back my own things is much of a bribe...)

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: These books on the floor... they're a complete mess. And this one, didn't he say it was an out-of-print collectible? It's completely covered in dust, and some of its pages have even fallen out...

dialogues.speaker: Kaveh
dialogues.text: *sigh* Guess I should help him repair it. This one too... And this one...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Local Sumpter Beasts, imported goods! Such a bright future ahead — I can picture the Mora just rolling in...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hehe, hahaha... ahahaha!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: You do realize you sound like a choking cow?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: It's called being imposing! Can't you feel it? Are you NOT intimidated?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Oh, I'm positively shaking in my sandals. What commands do you have for me, O mighty Lord Sangemah Bay?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Y—You... Ugh, you've got a lot of nerve, Nefer! You went and told Candace and the others everything, didn't you?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Seriously, do you have any idea how differently they see me now!?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Surely that's a good thing? I presume they're more disposed to actually like you now, maybe even view you as a friend.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: You traded my secret for sympathy! Thanks to you, I've lost every last shred of my mercantile majesty. How am I supposed to make anyone think I'm a big, scary investor now!?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: The dark days of Lord Sangemah Bay are behind you. Why not take this chance to make a few honest friends?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Hmph! Speaking of friends, since when did the notorious Lady Nefer gain such an admiration for holier-than-thou types? A Moonchanter here, an angel there... Hmph, who'd have thought it?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: A coming together of fates, nothing more. No need to throw around accusations of admiration.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Forget it. You're right about one thing, at least — making friends is never a bad thing for a merchant...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Still... *sob*... I really took a loss this time!

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: *sob*... Ugh, what are you looking at?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I'm trying to see if you're really crying or if those are just crocodile tears.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: A little birdy told me that when Lord Sangemah Bay makes money, the tears flow from the center of her eyes, but when she loses it, they flow from the corners. Which is it this time?

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Ugh, you're so annoying! I'm not talking to you anymore!

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Nefer! Thank goodness you're here. I've been looking everywhere for you.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Huh? Well well well, if it isn't the House of Daena's very own librarian! What can I offer you today, Miss Katayoun?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Oh, no, I'm not here to buy. I'm here to bring Lady Nefer a book, and a fascinating one at that. We agreed to meet at the entrance to The Mausoleum of King Deshret. One more thing, I bought this copy with my own money — it's not borrowed.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: "Reasoning Knows Not Time of Day, but Suspense Always Follows a Blizzard"... That's quite the mouthful...

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Huh! Isn't that... isn't that the one that...

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: It was all the rage for a while. People throughout the city were clamoring to get their hands on a copy. The names inside were all circled — everyone thought it was a riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Don't bring up that book in my presence! I don't even want to hear its name! That thing was nothing but a scam!

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Surprisingly enough, I've actually heard of this book... though it doesn't seem of much consequence. So, what truth lies behind it?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: You're from the Vahumana, and you're asking ME what the truth is? I'd say the actual "truth" was about the least important part of the whole episode.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: I brought you this book because it probably has the most interesting backstory of any in the House of Daena's collection, at least in recent years. As for its quality... Well, you can judge that for yourself.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: Don't tell me it's actually any good?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: You may not know this, Lord Sangemah Bay, but Lady Nefer has a fondness for books with, how should I put this... mixed reviews.

dialogues.speaker: Dori
dialogues.text: No eye for good literature, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Perhaps she feels that bad books hide interesting secrets? But I shouldn't put words in her mouth. It's probably fair to say she prefers the conversations that books can spark over the substance of the books themselves...

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Suits my style as an intel broker, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Very interesting, thank you. I'll return it to you once I'm done reading.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: And as it happens, I have something for you, too.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: ...Incense?

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: I imagine you've already used up the incense I gave you last time? Here's some more. This batch is from Nod-Krai, so the scent won't be quite the same.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: Well, actually... I've been saving the incense you gave me. I couldn't bring myself to waste it without a special occasion.

dialogues.speaker: Katayoun
dialogues.text: But I'll... I'll gladly accept this, too! And I promise I'll use it this time.

dialogues.speaker: Nefer
dialogues.text: Katayoun, you haven't changed a bit.

dialogues.speaker: Party Poppers
dialogues.text: BOOM!

dialogues.speaker: Party Poppers
dialogues.text: BOOM!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Congratulations, Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Well done, Collei! After studying for so long, you've finally become a full-fledged ranger!

dialogues.speaker: Zaha Hadi
dialogues.text: Sure hasn't been easy for you, huh? This really is fantastic news.

dialogues.speaker: Cyrus
dialogues.text: All grown up! No longer a trainee, but an official Forest Ranger! Hoho, the next step is to secure tenure in the Akademiya!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Thanks, everyone! It's true, I'm an official Forest Ranger now.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Master Tighnari, thank you for your guidance and support. I wish Mr. Cyno were here so I could thank him, too.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Cyno had a matter to attend to at the Temple of Silence. I don't imagine he'll be back for some time. But don't worry, we can celebrate together once he's finished.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: I'm afraid the party will have to wait. Collei still has some matters to attend to first.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Collei? Is... Is everything alright?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: No no, it's not what you think! There's nothing wrong with my health — I just have a few things I need to deal with.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #I've made plans with {NICKNAME} and Paimon to visit Mondstadt. Master Tighnari and Mr. Cyno will be accompanying us, too.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Well, that's a relief. Let's get together when everyone's back. I'm sure you'll be doing even better by then.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Of course. I have a feeling you're right.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: A few days later...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whew! After all that catching up on sleep and food, Paimon's feeling full of vim and vigor again!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: For someone who spends so much time resting, your recovery routine is surprisingly simple.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey, Paimon's been working her butt off too, you know! She flew all over the city helping everyone out.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't worry, I saw how hard you worked.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hehe. Alright, we all know you're the most hard-working person in Teyvat. As long as you're rested and full, that's what really matters.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's been looking around the place, and it seems like the city's already on the mend! But Paimon's been wondering how Nahida's doing... We should check in on her!

talks.objective: Go to the Sanctuary of Surasthana

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey Nahida! And Hat Guy's here, too!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: What's going on here?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Nothing much. Nahida was just expressing concern for my physical and mental well-being.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Oh, {NICKNAME} told Paimon all about that. We've both been very worried about you... Are you feeling alright?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: You make it sound like I'm on the brink of some kind of breakdown. Truth is, I'm doing much better than you might imagine.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: If we can just get to the bottom of Dottore's intentions, we can minimize his negative influence. That's the sort of thing I excel at.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Just listen to that newfound optimism! It seems like having you enroll in the Vahumana was a truly inspired move. I can really see the positive influence.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Observe, a classic Sumeru specialty — chalking everything up to education and learning.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: To be honest, even I can sense the change in you.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Everything Dottore said to you was a way to manipulate your mind. Fortunately, you're no longer under his sway.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Can someone as old as me really continue to grow...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: If it helps, just think of yourself as a late bloomer. It's all a matter of phrasing, and it comes down to what standards you measure yourself by.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: For a puppet, developing at such an age is perfectly normal. But if you choose to call yourself a late bloomer, it sounds more like... you consider yourself human.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: However you see yourself, well done!

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Alright, I see what you mean.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Anyway... What's your next step?

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: What else can I do but complete my current courses? Everything else can wait.

dialogues.speaker: Wanderer
dialogues.text: Anyway, that's enough chit-chat. There are still things in the city I need to help out with. I'll be heading there now.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon's so happy that Hat Guy is doing better than we thought, hehe.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But... What about you, Nahida? How are you holding up?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Pyro Gnosis burned down the corrupted Irminsul. The flames blazed for seven days and seven nights before they finally subsided. All that was left were the parts underground.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Now, Aaru shoulders the responsibilities that once belonged to Irminsul. The situation was contained before it got out of hand, so Teyvat's most vital information has largely been preserved.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Irminsul has a strong influence over you, doesn't it? How will you cope now that it's gone?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There's no need to worry. Thanks to Nicole's extraordinary talents, my connection to Irminsul has been severed and transposed onto Aaru.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Angels can do things like that!?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: They can. Such abilities are precisely what makes them so powerful. The Goddess of Flowers, Nabu Malikata, once claimed that she, too, could perform feats beyond the reach of mere mortals.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: In my eyes, much of what she went on to achieve reached such transcendent levels. Her and Nicole really are both fascinating and magnificent.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: So, does that mean your situation is stable now?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Correct. Just imagine that Aaru has become the new Irminsul, and the essence of my existence has been bound to it.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The wisdom of Sumeru has ultimately converged into a single, unified entity. Should we ascribe this all to fate, or is it merely fortune?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whatever it is, the important thing is that you're okay, Nahida.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: #Dendro Archon! Lesser Lord Kusanali! Oh, thank goodness you're here. Ah, greetings, {NICKNAME} and Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Sir Naphis, do you have something urgent to say?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Yes, there's something I need to report. We've received a message from Snezhnaya.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Naphis hands a letter to Nahida, who reads it...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The Fatui Harbinger "The Rooster" sends us his sympathies, along with all the usual pleasantries...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: His stance is that, following the unrest in Nod-Krai, Dottore was subjected to internal censure. This madness was the act of a rogue element, one who cannot be seen to represent the Zapolyarny Palace.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: No less than can be expected...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Snezhnaya paid a heavy price working to stop him. They even lost one of their own Harbingers.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The letter goes on to say that even so, Snezhnaya cannot claim to be blameless. Apparently, they will deal with Dottore's subordinates in accordance with Snezhnayan law, holding all those involved in his crimes accountable.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Additionally, they are supplying relief funds and supplies, which are already on route. They hope this will aid in Sumeru's reconstruction.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hmph! Sounds like he's got an answer for everything.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: True... But as diplomatic rhetoric goes, it's highly effective. Completely watertight, both in logic and sentiment.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: This disaster has had a profound impact on Sumeru. There is much that I will keep in my heart.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: The matter of Dottore can be seen as settled for now. We are sure to cross paths again in the future, and in that light, Snezhnaya would do well to uphold their responsibilities and keep a tight rein over their actions.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: With Irminsul burned, the flow of fate now carries many more possibilities. I will be watching carefully.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Perhaps... we can move on to a less serious matter? Dendro Archon, will you eat with us once this matter is dealt with? Everyone wishes to celebrate together. Your presence would be most welcome.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Of course! Dunyarzad, Cyno, and Haypasia all told me the same thing. If there isn't enough room for everyone, we can arrange back-to-back feasts!

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: What a wonderful idea! That just leaves the question of what we should eat...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Not more tomatoes, surely?

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: More? Dendro Archon, what do you mean by "more tomatoes"?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Those good friends of yours are always talking about tomatoes. Sometimes, when I'm walking through the city, I can even hear them arguing in the fields. Since you see them so often, you must hear about tomatoes even more than I do.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Tomatoes... Tomatoes... The word has a certain magic to it. Like the autumn fur of a Sumpter Beast, swirling in the wind, sometimes flying up my nose.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: ...Tomatoes... What can we make with tomatoes? Hmm... Wait, why tomatoes?

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #Take your time, there's no need to rush. {NICKNAME}, Paimon, and I still have somewhere we need to visit. You'll have plenty of time to think it over before I return.

dialogues.speaker: Naphis
dialogues.text: Does this mean you're going to Natlan? Meeting them there in person... It will require a long journey.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: I know. But this is necessary. I must go myself.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, we'll set off as soon as you're ready. Is that alright?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Sure! We'll be ready whenever you are.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You'll hear no objections from Paimon! We should grab some snacks along the way, though! It'll be just like going on a long holiday!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Wonderful! I'm looking forward to this so much!

talks.objective: Go to the Stadium of the Sacred Flame in Natlan

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Natlan is such a lively place!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It's super cheerful and positive too!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Mmhmm, I can see that. There are people outside exercising at all hours... Such a healthy way of life!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You came? Welcome, welcome! You must be hungry from your journey. Would you like something to eat?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Thanks, but no thanks! We've been eating the whole way here! We had a Mushroom Platter, Sabz Meat Stew, Butter-Braised Chicken, Padisarah Pudding... Paimon's positively stuffed!

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Alright, alright! No need for all that detail — I'm starting to get hungry myself...

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Maybe later, then. We can wait till everyone's got an appetite, then all head out for a meal together.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Hehe, sounds like a plan. Let's find somewhere to sit down.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: I should tell you, I already have some sense of why you've come.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Why's that, Mavuika?

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: To say thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Your senses are spot on. But on top of that, we also feel guilty.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Because the Pyro Gnosis has vanished? Mm, I sensed its loss.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Despite scouring through the remnants of Irminsul, we couldn't find any sign of the Pyro Gnosis... not even any trace of it burning to ash.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: That's certainly unusual. Still, the potential fallout from Irminsul's loss is significant, to say the least. Perhaps the Pyro Gnosis's disappearance is simply a knock-on effect of the impact it's had on a certain strand of fate.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: There's no need to feel guilty. We were clear that this time, there was to be no "returning" — only "giving," pure and simple.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: "Thank you" really is a fascinating phrase. We use it to express gratitude for the smallest of things, yet when faced with a kindness too immense to describe, we use exactly the same words.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: It's not that we lack other means of expression — it's that when we truly need to express our feelings, the simplest and purest words are always the most powerful.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: You're right. In Natlan, we prefer simple expressions too. "Companionship," "friendship," "support"... they might not sound fancy, but the sentiment behind them is sincere.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: That's wonderful to hear! Sincere feelings are often a vehicle for the deepest wisdom of all.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Irminsul's destruction doesn't seem to have done you much harm. I'm glad to see you're doing well.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: There's still a lot of work to do, but before we begin, we felt it was important to come here and speak with you.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Partly to express our gratitude, but also because we felt... that seeing you, in a sense, is like basking in warm sunlight.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Haha, that's a nice way of putting it. I like that.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: To tell you the truth, though, I'm not a fan of somber meetings. So, since there's nothing more to say, why don't we go bask in some actual sunlight? The weather's beautiful today.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What a great idea! Paimon's gonna lie back and soak up some rays!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Hah...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: In that case, I think I'll lie down for a bit too before we head to our next stop.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: And where might that be?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Mondstadt.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Paimon and I are gonna head back there with Collei and the gang.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Long ago, I sensed that the god remains inside Collei had come from the Goddess of Flowers, but I kept it a secret.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Those remains weren't hurting Collei, not as she is now — they simply exist. Besides, I could sense a deep yearning within her.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: A yearning... for an ordinary life. A yearning to hold onto the hard-won happiness she now enjoys. With someone like her, I have a responsibility to keep her secret.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She should be ready to face the truth by now.

dialogues.speaker: Mavuika
dialogues.text: Whenever people meet, there is always the potential to create warmth and kindness. Every child grows up, but even as adults, they are still children in the eyes of certain people.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh! Just like how Paimon sometimes sees Nahida as a little kid!

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Is that so? Well, anyone who's friends with a kid is probably a kid themselves.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course, and there's nothing wrong with that! When we get back, we'll actually be hanging out with another of our friends who happens to be a kid — or, more like looking after, in her case. Anyway, we'll always be there to watch out for our friends!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Dear Sucrose, when you receive this letter, I'll probably be as busy as always... but busy with wonderful things. That's because I'm no longer a trainee — I'm now an official Forest Ranger!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Impressive, right? Cyno said that official rangers sound much tougher than trainees. Though, he did say I was already pretty tough to start out with.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You probably heard that something big happened in Sumeru recently. Don't worry, it's all been taken care of. We're heading to Mondstadt soon, so if you're free, maybe we could meet up?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Plus, it's not just me — a few of us are going. Hey, do you still remember that time we all got together? You know, when we all went to the Windblume Festival. It'll be just like that!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Two days later, by the gates of Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Tighnari, is that...

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Don't you say it! Is that the Great "Vay-iew-vyastra"? Behold the Great Vayuvyastra, General Mahamatra.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: How times have changed. I wasn't expecting you to beat me to the punchline... You've changed!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: You've really upped the aggression in your battle against Cyno's jokes!

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Collei! How did you know what I was going to say!?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: For the love of...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hey—!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, you're right on time.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: I hope we haven't kept you waiting?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Collei!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Sucrose! It's been so long! How have you been?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: I've been well! Everything's going great. What about you? Are you still busy?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Not at the moment. Oh, right, that juicer you gave us works amazing! Faruzan loves it!

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Seriously? That's wonderful! I don't suppose you drew up a detailed test report? Oh! What fruits did you use? How was the texture of the final product?

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Sucrose, you might want to try asking your questions one at a time...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Albedo! Paimon didn't see you there!

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: It's been a while since all of us were together like this. How about we follow the same plan as last time?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Good idea, my friend, you never disappoint.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: So, what are your "identities" this time?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: Don't remind him...

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Ahem... First things first, allow me to introduce our very own "official" Forest Ranger Collei. The rest of us are simply her humble travel companions.

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: This sounds like one of those mushy stories that gets people hooked on some corny, heart-warming premise.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Oh, is our story not heart-warming? If I recall correctly, there was even a scene like this in King of Invokations.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Besides being heartwarming, our story's also about tough, impressive-sounding job titles! Uhm... At least... that's what I think.

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: You, Collei, and the others meet with the Knights of Favonius. After exchanging warm greetings, you head to the library, where you run into...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Oh! You're here already? I'm still giving Dodoco a little trim. I won't be a moment.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A trim? Does Dodoco need haircuts, too?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Of course! It's important to know how to take loving care of the apples of your eye!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hehe. All of these trivial matters get left to me. It's because I'm an angel, and angels are, in a way, the guardians of all Teyvat.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ohhh, right. Well, that's definitely an impressive-sounding job title!

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: What are you writing?

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: I'm just brainstorming some cool-sounding lines.

dialogues.speaker: Albedo
dialogues.text: Oh! Write them on these card backs.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Of course!

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Ahem! Clearly, my lines are pretty amazing, wouldn't you say?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Collei, you seem a little nervous.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I was just wondering... who was the person you mentioned who needed their wish fulfilled?

dialogues.speaker: Tighnari
dialogues.text: ...Wish? What do you mean?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole asked if we could meet up in Mondstadt once everything was over. She said a friend of hers had a wish that needed my help to come true.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: Well, you never mentioned that before. All we knew was that you'd arranged to meet in Mondstadt. But we thought it had something to do with the god remains.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hmm... To be fair, everything I told you was true. Anyway, my friend is waiting.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Come on, let's pay her a visit.

talks.objective: Go beneath the great tree at Windrise

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh, you're...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Surprised? I bet you weren't expecting to meet a woman like me beneath this beautiful tree in a faraway land.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: "An oasis will spring from the place where a Jinn resides..." That saying falls somewhat flat here in Mondstadt, given that everywhere is already so lush and green.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Liloupar!? What are you doing here?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I made friends with Miss Nicole. I asked her to bring me here and then invite Collei to come.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: The prologue to this story is that I have a wish. It has stirred within my heart for centuries, millennia even. Originally, it was merely Al-Ahmar's lie, but now it has become reality.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Could this be...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...related to the Goddess of Flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My dear young lady... My mistress left her final trace in this world upon you. I can't tell you how glad I am to see you here.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: And now I have seen you... and peered into your heart. You have experienced hardships and suffered setbacks. The torment an ordinary person might expect to face has befallen you threefold. This is the source of your resilience.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: But, beneath all this, I've witnessed the seeds of desire. You yearn to return to the simple life you once knew, do you not?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...I do. I want to throw away everything that isn't mine.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: But how do you decide what is yours? The scars that others carve into your flesh, the kindness and love they inscribe, are these things not yours as well?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: They are. This is something I've talked about with Miss Nicole.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Miss Nicole said I should learn how to adjust my standards. I just want to live as an ordinary human. Anything beyond that isn't mine.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Hehe... Don't you want anything from the remains of the Goddess of Flowers?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: She gave me a revelation once. I think that's already more than enough.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: In the past, you would not have possessed such a rich heart. Your brief life has taught you to hold on to everything good, to home in on kindness...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: How fascinating. You're nothing like Nabu Malikata, and you're certainly not her.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: O—Of course not... I'm not some great and powerful being, Miss Liloupar.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Yet I am a Jinn. We exist because of the Lord of Flowers. We revere and love her. My wish is to see her one last time, to give everything for her.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Collei, can you do this for me?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But... Her remains won't be easy to remove. Are you sure this is what you want?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: That's beside the point. First, I need to know, are you willing to do something for the soul of this lonely, wandering woman?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I... I'm willing.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: But look, you know nothing about me. Even if you have heard the stories about me, all you would know is that I was rightly punished for the many evil deeds I committed.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: So you do know. Your lips are quivering, your eyes trembling... and still you're willing to do something for me. Life has been cruel to you, and yet you've learned to be kind.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My dear young lady, to repay your kindness, I too must play my part.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Are you sure about this, Liloupar?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: I yearn to see my mistress. For this moment, the world can burn to ashes, the universe be engulfed in flame... I care about nothing else.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: And you, Collei, I can give you a gift. You'll become just another ordinary human.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But Miss Liloupar, what will happen to you?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: My wish will be fulfilled, and I can die happy.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Why would you wish for that!?

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: A long, unending life might seem desirable for one who has never possessed it, yet it brings torment to one who has. My remains are scattered across the yellow sands, but my soul can find no peace.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Since you've promised to grant my wish, give me that release. Allow the dying to die, and let the dead rest in peace. You have my thanks.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Collei, there's no pressure on you. What she said... It's all true. A wish is a genuine desire, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: It's as if you want to use the last of your life to give me a better future...

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Nothing so selfless. We'll be using our futures to fulfill each other's wishes. This is a noble act, a beautiful and secret transaction between two women.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I understand... Miss Liloupar, I'm ready.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: Close your eyes, Collei. Then open your soul. From there, I will embrace my mistress.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: The downpour of flowers is your touch. Like returning to the very beginning... Like surrendering to your grace. My mistress.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: People say that devotion is beautiful, yet filled with pain. How foolish of them. For me, devotion is beautiful, pure, and painless. Devotion is my love.

dialogues.speaker: Liloupar
dialogues.text: ...Thank you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Liloupar... She disappeared?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: The Jinn's magic bottle falls silently to the ground, now completely empty.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: She left, carrying the blessing of flowers.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Collei, are you alright?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...I'm fine. Now that the remains are gone, I...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: ...Don't actually feel any different at all.

dialogues.speaker: Nahida
dialogues.text: Those remains weren't hurting Collei, not as she is now — they simply exist. Besides, I could sense a deep yearning within her.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: (Collei must have already received what she was yearning for.)

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I'm doing fine. I feel relaxed. There's really no need to worry.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Then my wish has come true, too.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: To become ordinary?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Hehe, that's just one of my wishes. Actually, I have a few more. For instance, I want to protect the people I meet and help them find happiness... that sort of thing.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: So between Miss Liloupar and me, you've fulfilled two wishes already, and protected two people.

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: Wonderful, isn't it? I feel so fantastically happy!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I guess that settles things here.

dialogues.speaker: Cyno
dialogues.text: So, what's next? What do you want to do when we get back to town?

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Collei, look who I've brought to see you!

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Hey, Collei! I heard you guys were holding some kind of secret event. How come you started without me?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Huh? Oh, no, it's nothing like that! We were... just saying goodbye to an old friend.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: Really? Who?

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Me. The old me.

dialogues.speaker: Amber
dialogues.text: So that's what this is all about... Did you come all the way to Mondstadt for that? Because we knew the old you, so we could witness the change...

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Exactly. The old me is gone. I puffed her into the air, and she became a fluffy pink cloud, floating into the sky, before disappearing forever.

dialogues.speaker: Sucrose
dialogues.text: Do you think... maybe up in the sky, she has friends waiting for her with test tubes, flasks, and bows?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh... When you put it like that, it doesn't sound so bad after all!

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: What do you think, Miss Nicole?

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: I think, maybe that's right...

dialogues.speaker: Nicole
dialogues.text: At least... if it were up to me, I'd consider that a happy ending.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Dear Sucrose, even though my childhood ended long ago, these past few days have really felt like growing up again. I've become stronger, and I feel like I can finally accomplish things by myself.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: Surely someone as mysterious as you will find a friend like this fascinating? Always growing, always thriving like a plant.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: I came to say goodbye to my old self. I know that after this, she'll be gone. Thinking about it makes me feel a little lonely... I know the weakness that kept me company will one day leave me too.

dialogues.speaker: Collei
dialogues.text: But somewhere in my heart, I feel a great sense of joy. It feels like I've always wanted to take this step — to walk towards the new me.
